stories.label: Ukraine falls behind Moldova on path to EU membership
stories.summary: Kyiv and Chisinau applied together, but the European Commission's enlargement report now proposes different end dates for their membership talks, and blames Ukraine's sputtering anti-corruption effort. Lead with the decoupling: a country at war is told its courts and graft bodies, not the front line, set its pace. Add the wider Balkan picture (Montenegro praised, stagnation elsewhere) from Balkan Insight.

stories.label: Election stiffens the Fed's guardrails, but independence risks remain
stories.summary: A Democratic Senate takes the confirmation gate for Fed governors away from Trump: the Banking Committee (with Elizabeth Warren's camp ascendant) can now block nominees picked to push rates down. Lead with the mechanism — appointments, not speeches, are how a president bends a central bank — and what remains exposed before January. Name the Fed funds rate and the US 10-year Treasury yield.

stories.label: Eurozone inflation rises to 4% in October
stories.summary: Eurozone inflation reached 4% in October, driven by fossil-fuel prices from the Iran war, while the Bank of England's new 'sticky' gauge shows UK pressures not yet building ahead of its meeting this week. Lead with the divergence: energy shock feeds through to the euro area first, which puts the ECB rate and a December hike (floated by the Bundesbank's Nagel) on the table. Name the ECB rate and the euro.

stories.label: Oil prices tumble below $100 on post-election peace hopes
stories.summary: Brent crude fell below $100 to a two-month low as traders priced the Democratic landslide as pressure on Trump to end the Iran war; JD Vance blamed the defeat on anger over the war. Lead with the mechanism: a vote in Washington moved the war-risk premium on Gulf barrels, a day after tankers burned in Hormuz. Name Brent crude, WTI and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz; note that importers like Pakistan cut pump prices the same day.

stories.label: American Voters Overwhelmingly Reject AI Data Centers
stories.summary: Data centers were on the ballot in dozens of local measures and races, and lost most of them; in Texas, governor-elect Gina Hinojosa ousted Greg Abbott pledging to crack down on server-warehouse growth. Lead with the count of measures lost, then the mechanism: power bills, water and grid connections turned AI infrastructure into a local voting issue. Consequence: Wall Street cut targets for bitcoin miners and data-center builders, while miners already holding approved power connections may gain.

stories.label: French blood banks targeted by refrigerator cyberattack
stories.summary: Attackers tried to destroy stored blood plasma by driving cold-storage temperatures past boiling, in a wave of attacks on refrigeration control systems across several European countries on Sunday and Monday, French authorities said. Lead with the target: not data but physical medical stock, through the internet-connected controllers that run cold chains. Who is exposed (hospitals, supermarkets) and who is suspected.

stories.label: War, drought, inflation: How Sudan is edging closer to famine
stories.summary: Poor seasonal harvests and runaway inflation are compounding three years of SAF-RSF war, pushing millions of Sudanese toward famine. Lead with the convergence: war cut planting, drought cut yields, and the collapsing pound priced what remains out of reach. Name who blocks access and who holds the routes; continuation of the siege is the development.

stories.label: Opposition leaders gather at JUI-F chief Fazl's Islamabad residence to discuss KP emergency
stories.summary: Pakistan's opposition, PTI included, convened at Maulana Fazlur Rehman's residence over the imposition of an emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the province PTI governs. Lead with the power move: Islamabad suspending an elected provincial government, and the constitutional mechanism used. Who loses representation, and whether the opposition alliance can contest it.

stories.label: Inflación, sequía y alza de costos de producción presionan los precios de los alimentos y las familias hondureñas recortan sus compras
stories.summary: Fuel costs from the Iran war, an El Niño drought and rising production costs are pushing food prices up in Honduras: inflation hit 6.28% in September and 1.8 million Hondurans face crisis or emergency food insecurity. Lead with the market-stall view — families cutting and substituting — then the chain from a war in the Gulf to a Tegucigalpa farmers' fair.

stories.label: Q&A: What is in the global ‘roadmap’ for transitioning away from fossil fuels?
stories.summary: Brazil's COP30 presidency has released a first-of-its-kind global roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels, alongside a separate roadmap to end deforestation. Lead with what it actually asks of producers and who signed on, and what it lacks: no binding dates. The angle for this reader: Gulf petrostates and Indonesia's forests are the two places it bites. Filed as politics: a policy document, not a finding.

stories.label: NASA's Swift Observatory Is Crashing Back to Earth Today After 21 Years in Orbit
stories.summary: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, the 3,200-pound gamma-ray-burst hunter, re-enters the atmosphere after 21 years. Lead with what science loses: Swift's rapid slewing found and localised thousands of gamma-ray bursts and fed follow-up of gravitational-wave events, and no replacement with that response time is flying. Note the orbit decayed under high solar activity. Keep it factual and cite NASA's own figures, not the outlet's framing.

stories.label: Hermes Agent手机端要来了！能读取手机数据，内测名额秒没
stories.summary: Nous Research's open-source Hermes Agent opened a mobile beta whose 'Device Access' feature lets agents read the phone's calendar, contacts, location and health data — sent on to the user's server and the AI provider behind it. Lead with that data flow, then the pricing ($0.60-2.50 a day for cloud-hosted agents) and the race with OpenClaw's poorly received app. Reported from China's developer community by Zhidx.

stories.label: Ukrainian news outlet Kyiv Independent hit by suspected Russian cyberattack
stories.summary: A suspected Russian cyberattack took down the website of The Kyiv Independent, one of Ukraine's main English-language outlets — days after a destructive attack on Russian host Beget. Lead with the target: the outlet foreign readers rely on for the war, hit as US-mediated talks approach in Abu Dhabi. Attack type, duration and attribution evidence.

stories.label: Elon Musk's $500 Million Bet Fails to Help Republicans
stories.summary: The world's richest man spent nearly $500 million on Republican candidates, a record for one donor, and the candidates he backed lost, Ken Paxton's Texas Senate race (the most expensive in US history) among them. Lead with what that money bought: almost nothing. The mechanism: unlimited super PAC spending after Citizens United lets one fortune buy airtime but not votes when the war and fuel prices are driving them. Al Jazeera notes Musk made light of the defeats. Do not repeat the overall results already covered; this is the story of money in politics.

stories.label: Firsts for women and minorities in US midterm elections
stories.summary: New since our 3 November story on the Islamophobic closing pitch in Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed won the Senate seat, about 52% to 46%, and becomes the first Muslim US senator, after AIPAC-linked super PACs spent a record $30.6 million against him in the primary and at least $12.7 million in the general. Lead with El-Sayed and that spending; then list the other firsts for women and minorities. Dateline Michigan.

stories.label: Iran supreme leader says those expecting US policy shift 'seriously mistaken'
stories.summary: Hours after the Democratic sweep, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei told Iranians not to expect any change in US behaviour, while adviser Mohammad Mokhber claimed Iran had won by shifting the war's costs onto the United States and spokesman Baghaei said Iran would not be intimidated. Lead with Tehran's line: the vote changes nothing. The mechanism: a Democratic Congress can cut war funding when government funding runs out on 11 December, but the war powers stay with Trump until January. Attribute the Mehr quotes to Iranian state media. Tie it to the Doha talks and to the five conditions Tehran set this week.

stories.label: Короли асфальта. С кем связаны фирмы, «провалившие» ремонт дорог в Бишкеке?
stories.summary: Kloop's investigation: Bishkek spent at least 740 million som rebuilding the Auezov Street bridge and parts of Baitik Baatyr and Akhunbaev streets, and the new asphalt sagged and slid within months. Two of the three contractors are tied to former and current officials, and the city ignores complaints. Lead with the money and the tie to officials. The mechanism is procurement capture: officials award public works to firms they are connected to, and no one answers for the failure. Kyrgyzstan dateline.

stories.label: Segurança Pública: PEC da redução da maioridade penal no Senado pode ter relator do PT
stories.summary: Brazil's Senate has passed the Public Security constitutional amendment, and a second amendment lowering the age of criminal responsibility may be taken up on Wednesday, possibly with a rapporteur from Lula's own PT. Lead with who would be affected: teenagers, overwhelmingly Black and poor, moved into an adult prison system already over capacity. The mechanism: a tough-on-crime push before the 2026 vote, and a governing party weighing whether to steer the amendment or resist it. Brazil dateline.

stories.label: Tinubu's ADC seeks arrest of Kwara lawyer over alleged land grabbing
stories.summary: President Tinubu's aide-de-camp, Lt-Col Nurudeen Yusuf, who is also a traditional ruler in Kwara State, has started criminal defamation proceedings against lawyer Nuruddin Abdulsalam and is seeking his arrest, after Abdulsalam accused him of land grabbing and abuse of power. Lead with the inversion: the man accused of taking land is the one asking police to arrest his accuser. The mechanism: criminal defamation, which press-freedom groups have long asked Nigeria to repeal, still lets officials put critics in jail. Kwara, Nigeria dateline.

stories.label: Democratic sweep adds new twist to markets' Iran, AI, and debt worries
stories.summary: Reuters from London: a divided Washington is the newest problem for markets already dealing with the Iran war's oil shock, an AI boom pushing up growth and inflation, and the US debt load. Gold jumped about 3% to above $4,060 an ounce on Comex (TASS figures). Lead with gold and the US 10-year Treasury yield, and say why: gridlock over spending and the debt ceiling against a war-driven inflation risk. Do not repeat the dollar/yen move already covered. Dateline London.

stories.label: Bitcoin briefly sinks to $75,700 as bets on a Democratic sweep rattle markets
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to about $75,700 as the returns came in, because Democrats oppose the CLARITY Act, the crypto industry's market-structure bill, and a Democratic Congress can now stall it and question stablecoin policy. The industry spent heavily for a friendly Congress and lost. Lead with the bill, not the price; chart bitcoin. Merge CoinDesk's analyst roundup on the blue Congress for what changes for stablecoins.

stories.label: Tokenization news: $1.1T Schroders brings emerging market bond fund to Solana
stories.summary: Schroders, a 200-year-old London manager with $1.1 trillion under management, is putting an emerging-market bond fund on the public Solana blockchain. That takes Wall Street's tokenization push from money-market funds into the debt of developing countries. Lead with what it changes: holders of Global South sovereign and corporate debt could trade around the clock on a public chain, and who carries the custody and settlement risk is still untested. London dateline.

stories.label: Smiling can make you happier—unless someone forces you to do it
stories.summary: Nicholas Coles, whose own research was cited as evidence that forcing a smile lifts your mood, tested that result again and found the effect disappears when people are told to smile. Lead with a scientist checking and narrowing his own famous finding. This is the replication crisis in psychology working as it should, and it bears on every self-help and wellness claim built on the original result.

stories.label: 英伟达团队下场！国产视频模型开源，硅谷公司上门谈授权
stories.summary: An Nvidia team and the US video start-up Pika are both building on MiniMax's open-weight Chinese video model H3, which has passed 24 million downloads and 300 derivative models, and Nvidia's project involves a commercial licence from MiniMax. The surprise is in the licence: the free community licence excludes the US, the EU, the UK and South Korea, so Western firms have to negotiate with a Chinese lab, and any user earning over $20 million a year needs written permission. Lead with the reversal: Silicon Valley building on Chinese open weights. China dateline.

stories.label: Cyberattack wipes cloud data at major Russian hosting provider Beget
stories.summary: A cyberattack destroyed data across the cloud infrastructure of Beget, one of Russia's largest hosting providers, and hundreds of websites are down while it tries to restore them. Lead with the wiper: this was destruction, not ransom. Say who has claimed it, if anyone, and where it fits in the cyber front of the Ukraine war, where hitting one shared host takes out thousands of businesses at once. Russia dateline.

stories.label: Bezahlkarte für Asylsuchende: Berlin setzt Bargeld-Obergrenze aus
stories.summary: Berlin has suspended the cash withdrawal cap on the payment card asylum seekers must use, which limited how much of their own benefit they could take out in cash in a city where many shops and services do not take cards. The Berlin Refugee Council calls it a partial victory. Lead with how the card works: a payment system designed to control what refugees can spend. Whether the card is scrapped altogether now depends on Berlin's coalition talks. Berlin dateline.

stories.label: Four oil tankers destroyed in Hormuz after hitting mines, Tehran says
stories.summary: New development since yesterday's IRGC claim of three tankers hit: Tehran now says four tankers are ablaze and destroyed, a day after Trump announced US strikes on Iran, while mediated talks show little progress. Lead with the escalation from damage to destruction, then who owns and crews the ships and what it does to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Attribute the mine claim to the IRGC; the figure is Tehran's, not independently confirmed.

stories.label: Government yet to identify those behind alleged wiretapping: Minister
stories.summary: Someone wiretapped Indonesia's president and senior officials; a general has been arrested and the military has deployed thousands of troops to secure Jakarta, yet the state secretary says the government still does not know who did it. Lead with the troops on the capital's streets and the arrest, then the civil-military question: who holds power over the police and army under Prabowo, and what the deployment signals for Indonesia's democracy.

stories.label: Tracing the recruitment trap behind Russia’s war
stories.summary: Bangladeshi men paid agents for promised civilian jobs in Russia and ended up on the Ukraine front line; families now wait for bodies and want the recruiters prosecuted. Lead with the money paid and the bait-and-switch, then the mechanism: a labour-migration pipeline that feeds Russia's army with men from poor Muslim-majority countries, and what Dhaka has (or hasn't) done to stop it. Dateline Bangladesh.

stories.label: Blue tsunami breaks MAGA: 5 takeaways from a blowout midterm election
stories.summary: New since the Senate call: the House has now been called for the Democrats, so they hold both chambers, and flips in Texas (Talarico, the first Democrat to win statewide since 1994), Kansas (first Democratic senator in almost a century), Maine and South Carolina show how far the vote reached. Lead with the scale, a repudiation compared to 1974, and the cause voters named: the Iran war and fuel prices. What a Democratic Congress can now block: war funding, tariffs, Israel aid.

stories.label: Trump's midterm rebuke gives trading partners room to resist
stories.summary: The midterm result is read in Seoul, Tokyo, New Delhi and Beijing as a weakened hand on tariffs: governments that were negotiating under pressure may now stall, waiting for a Congress less willing to back the trade war. Lead with what India specifically gains and risks (Russian oil penalties, H-1B visas, per News18 and Bloomberg), and the mechanism: tariffs raised US consumer prices, and those prices cost Trump the vote. Dateline Seoul/New Delhi, not Washington.

stories.label: Copper and conflict trigger record profits for Japan's commodity traders
stories.summary: Four of Japan's biggest trading houses (Mitsui among them) posted record profits on the energy turmoil from the Iran war and surging copper prices. Lead with who profits from the war's price shock while importers and households pay for it; name copper and Brent crude, the series we chart. Mitsui's chief warns the risks are 'unpredictable rather than calming down'.

stories.label: Sindh cabinet approves new price of wheat at Rs4,500 per 40kg
stories.summary: New decision following yesterday's story on imported wheat failing to cut Karachi flour prices: Sindh's cabinet cut the wheat release price by Rs500 to Rs4,500 per 40kg and ordered flour mills to pass the cut on to consumers. Lead with whether the order has teeth: who enforces it on the mills, and whether bread prices follow. Name wheat, the series we chart.

stories.label: Vonovia sharply criticizes Berlin's possible apartment expropriation plans
stories.summary: Berlin's likely new government, led by far-left mayoral candidate Elif Eralp, has pledged to expropriate large landlords' apartments, and Germany's biggest landlord Vonovia calls it legally questionable. Lead with the stakes: a European capital moving to socialise housing owned by listed corporations, the 2021 referendum that backed it, and who pays (tenants' rents versus compensation from the public purse).

stories.label: 17秒验明AI“真身”！Anthropic开源可证明推理系统，能抓模型调包
stories.summary: Anthropic open-sourced FlashProve, a zkSNARK system that lets an API user check on a CPU in about 17 seconds that an answer really came from the model they paid for, tested on the 400-billion-parameter Llama 4 Maverick. Lead with the problem it solves (providers swapping in a cheaper model, tampered outputs, regulators auditing compute use), then the cost: proving takes 70-95x the GPU time of normal inference and handles only 1,024-token contexts. Zhidx, a mainland outlet, reports it.

stories.label: ByteDance reportedly tightens access to Claude and Codex, even for employees paying out of pocket
stories.summary: Since the start of November ByteDance has been barring staff from using external AI coding tools, Claude and Codex, on company code and internal documents, even when employees pay for them themselves. Lead with that detail, then the mechanism: the leak risk of sending proprietary code to US labs, and the push toward in-house Chinese models as the US-China AI split deepens on both sides.

stories.label: Digitalgipfel: KI-Torschlusspanik
stories.summary: At Germany's federal Digital Summit, AI as an economic driver dominated, and the market industry wanted most was the public sector itself: government administration. Lead with who stands to win public AI contracts and what oversight, data-protection or sovereignty questions netzpolitik says are being skipped in the rush. Dateline Germany.

stories.label: Prostaglandin promotes tumor growth via inhibiting tumor antigen presentation in triple-negative breast cancer - Cell Death & Disease
stories.summary: Researchers found that prostaglandin helps triple-negative breast cancer hide from the immune system by suppressing tumour antigen presentation. Lead with the finding: the most aggressive breast cancer, with the fewest targeted drugs, may be helped by a molecule that common COX-inhibitor drugs block. Be clear that this is lab and preclinical work, not a treatment.

stories.label: Franc, Yen Emerge as FX Winners as US Midterms Weaken Dollar
stories.summary: The dollar had its worst day in a month in Asian trading as returns pointed to a Democratic Congress: the Swiss franc rose almost 1% and the yen 0.7%. Lead with the mechanism: markets are pricing a divided government that can constrain Trump's war spending and tariff agenda, and a weaker dollar eases import costs for Asian economies paying for oil at war prices. Name the yen and the dollar so the figures attach.

stories.label: Greenland parliament approves security deal with US, Denmark
stories.summary: Greenland's Inatsisartut voted 16-0, with seven abstentions, for the trilateral Arctic security agreement signed with Denmark and the US in September. Lead with the abstentions: a third of the chamber declined to back a deal that expands the US military footprint on an island Trump has said he wants to own. Explain what Nuuk gained or ceded in sovereignty and what the deal lets US forces do.

stories.label: Los tres jinetes MAGA en Honduras
stories.summary: Contracorriente maps the network tying the MAGA movement to Honduras: the Winklevoss twins, who gave more than $46 million to Trump and his agenda and invest in the Próspera charter city (ZEDE), plus ultraconservative evangelical pastors and lobbyists who broker access between Honduran politicians and Washington. Lead with the money and Próspera, the private enclave suing Honduras for billions after the country repealed the ZEDE law. Hondurans barely know these actors, yet they shape the country's politics.

stories.label: Unsafe Hostels, Other Facilities: How UNIJOS fails students with disabilities
stories.summary: A Premium Times investigation finds students with disabilities at the federal University of Jos crawling into hostel bathrooms and shut out of classrooms without ramps. Lead with the human detail, then the accountability gap: Nigeria's 2018 disability law gave public buildings five years to become accessible, and a federal university still is not. Name who is responsible for compliance and whether anyone has enforced it.

stories.label: Refinery audit may cut prices by Rs40-50/litre
stories.summary: Pakistan's petroleum dealers demand a forensic audit of the country's refineries, saying their profits have soared and that the audit could allow fuel price cuts of Rs40-50 a litre. Lead with who pays: with the Iran war holding Brent crude above $100, Pakistanis pay war prices at the pump while refiners' margins widen under a pricing formula the state sets. Explain the deemed-duty and margin mechanism, and name Brent crude.

stories.label: Cotton arrivals rise to 4.7m bales by Oct 31
stories.summary: Pakistan's cotton arrivals rose 6.9% to 4.74 million bales, but the recovery is fragile: sugarcane is displacing cotton in its traditional Punjab and Sindh belt and extreme heat is damaging fibre quality. Lead with the structural shift: a crop that feeds the textile industry, Pakistan's largest exporter, is losing land to a water-hungry crop favoured by sugar mill owners, many of them politicians. What it means for import bills and textile jobs.

stories.label: Kling’s $18 Billion Private Value Tops Parent Kuaishou’s Market Cap
stories.summary: Kuaishou closed a capital injection into its AI video unit Kling at a post-money valuation above $18 billion, more than the parent's own Hong Kong market value, with Tencent, Alibaba Cloud and Baidu all taking small stakes. Lead with the inversion: the subsidiary is worth more than the company that owns it. The angle from Beijing's tech press: China's rival platforms are co-investing in one video-generation model rather than each building their own.

stories.label: Contas espalham conteúdo falso sobre bets nas redes enquanto STF discute proibição
stories.summary: As Brazil's Supreme Court (STF) holds public hearings on banning online betting, Agência Pública found accounts on X spreading fabricated stories about betting while industry lobbyists filled the hearing. Lead with the coordination: what the posts claimed, how many accounts, and whether they trace back to the betting industry. The stakes: Brazilians lose billions a month to the 'bets', much of it from welfare recipients.

stories.label: Prototype X-BAT VTOL ‘Fighter’ Drone Unveiled
stories.summary: Shield AI showed the first prototype of X-BAT, a tail-sitting combat drone that takes off vertically with no runway and flies under its own AI pilot. Lead with the runway: an autonomous jet that can launch from a ship deck or a clearing removes the airbases an adversary would strike first. Explain what autonomy it claims and who is buying.

stories.label: Testing Einstein's laws from the bottom of the Mediterranean Sea
stories.summary: The KM3NeT collaboration used 5,828 atmospheric neutrinos caught by its ORCA telescope, deep in the Mediterranean off Toulon, to test Lorentz invariance, the principle that physics is the same in every direction and frame, which some quantum-gravity theories predict breaks down. Lead with the detector: a lattice of light sensors 2,450 metres under the sea. Say what limit they set and why a violation would matter.

stories.label: Iran commander sets out five conditions for regional security
stories.summary: New development after the Qeshm strikes we covered: Tehran now calls the US ceasefire proposal insufficient and a commander has named five conditions for any regional security deal. Lead with the conditions themselves and who they bind (US forces, Gulf hosts, the blockade), and what they mean for ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude as Qatari mediators fly to Tehran.

stories.label: Justice Department identifies potential targets in Alaska Senate probe
stories.summary: On election day itself, the Justice Department sent target letters to a prominent Democratic attorney and others over an Alaska Senate candidate who shares a name with Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. Lead with the timing: a criminal inquiry escalated while ballots are being cast, and who it touches. The accountability question is the department's own norm against overt steps near an election.

stories.label: IEC tightens security amid ballot disruptions, arrests and election intimidation
stories.summary: Hours before South Africa's local government elections on Wednesday, ballot storage sites have been targeted, election materials damaged and arrests made across several provinces. Lead with the attacks and where they happened, then who is accused (the MK party is named in the coverage) and how thousands of police are deployed. The stake is trust in a vote that decides who runs broke municipalities.

stories.label: Video | 1 Killed After 2 Helicopters Collide In Nepal While Landing
stories.summary: Two helicopters clipped rotors while landing near Everest base camp, killing an Indian tourist. Lead with the mechanism: a crowded landing zone served by many small operators in the autumn trekking season, and what Nepal's aviation regulator has done or not done about heli traffic in the Khumbu after past crashes.

stories.label: AMD Sales Forecast Tops Estimates on Soaring AI Chip Demand
stories.summary: AMD's shares fell 12% in the past week; tonight it forecast fourth-quarter revenue above estimates on data-centre AI chip demand. Lead with the forecast against that slide and how much of the growth rests on a few buyers (Meta, OpenAI) — the question is whether AMD's challenge to Nvidia is broadening or concentrating. Name AMD's share price as the series.

stories.label: Bundesbank's Nagel joins ECB chorus backing December rate hike
stories.summary: Bundesbank chief Joachim Nagel says a December ECB hike is almost inevitable, joining a long list of governors and making a third hike this year close to settled. Lead with why: energy-driven inflation from the Iran war, and who pays — indebted southern eurozone states and mortgage holders. Name the ECB deposit rate and euro-area inflation as the series.

stories.label: Joburg accused of using workers as 'political pawns' after it pushes through wage deal
stories.summary: Johannesburg signed a multibillion-rand wage deal for about 35,000 municipal workers on the eve of local elections, a deal experts say the financially distressed city cannot afford. Lead with the cost against the city's budget and the timing; the mechanism is the ANC-run metro buying union goodwill with money residents will pay for in services.

stories.label: Russia looks to hide data centers underground as Ukrainian drones strike back
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes have damaged Russian facilities housing AI supercomputers and knocked out cloud services for millions, and Russian firms are now moving data centres underground, including into old mines. Lead with the outages and who lost service; the structural point is that compute is now a war target, and hardening it costs what.

stories.label: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
stories.summary: The New York Times and other publishers sued Brave, alleging its browser bypasses paywalls and sells the news it strips to AI companies through its search API. Lead with the two demands — kill the paywall bypass, end the AI data deals — and why it is a new front: suing the pipe that feeds models, not the model makers.

stories.label: Google dismantles massive botnet hidden in Android TV boxes
stories.summary: Google took down the X.CPE botnet, built mostly from cheap Android TV set-top boxes plus telehealth devices, karaoke machines and digital signage. Lead with the device count and where the infected boxes are — usually in the Global South, sold preinfected — not with Google; the dateline belongs where the devices are. The mechanism is uncertified hardware shipping with malware from the factory.

stories.label: Servier's $1.55 billion muscular dystrophy drug fails first major test
stories.summary: Sevasemten, which Servier bought from Edgewise in June for $1.55 billion in cash, failed to slow Becker muscular dystrophy in a long placebo-controlled trial. Lead with the trial result and what it measured; the science point is what it says about targeting fast skeletal muscle myosin, and the patients left with no approved therapy.

stories.label: Trump says US will end military aid to Israel by year-end
stories.summary: On Fox & Friends on election morning, Trump said the US will stop its roughly $4bn a year in military aid to Israel at the end of 2026, calling it a 'bad talking point' and naming Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed. Lead with the gap between the claim and the paper: the current $3.8bn memorandum runs to 2028, Netanyahu has asked for a new ten-year deal, and nothing is signed. The mechanism to explain: Congress's proposed Section 219 would move support out of the MOU into Pentagon co-production and R&D programmes with less oversight (Responsible Statecraft, https://responsiblestatecraft.org/israel-aid-trump/, an advocacy outlet: attribute it). What's next: Netanyahu's reaction amid his own leadership fight, and whether Section 219 returns after the vote.

stories.label: Americans vote for new Congress members in US midterm election
stories.summary: Polls are open for all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats. Do not write a horse-race preview; the angle is how Republicans made anti-Muslim attacks their closing pitch, flooding Michigan's Senate race against Abdul El-Sayed with anti-Arab ads and using Islamophobia to sell the Iran war (New Lines reportage, Inkstick). Lead with the Michigan race as the test of whether that works, then what Democrats say they will investigate if they win the House (France 24). What's next: results tonight, Michigan first.

stories.label: Hoax bomb threats disrupt flights in Europe
stories.summary: Bomb threats hit at least seven planes across Europe in one day, shutting Warsaw Modlin after a London flight's unplanned landing; no explosives were found. Lead with the count and the coordination, and place it beside the same week's hacks of supermarket fridges across Europe: a pattern of cheap disruption aimed at infrastructure. Say who investigates and whether anyone is named; do not attribute without a source. TASS figures only as one source among several.

stories.label: Oil Prices record Fall
stories.summary: A day after Brent crude fell 8% below $104 on Iran diplomacy, it climbed back above $105 after US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island. The new development is the reversal: one night of strikes undid the diplomatic discount, because Qeshm sits on the Strait of Hormuz and its bases are what threaten shipping. Name Brent crude and WTI, and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz; say who pays the swing (importers in Asia, Gulf-dependent economies), with Emirates NBD's view that the diplomatic opening is now vulnerable.

stories.label: Amid deepening financial crisis, UNRWA conducts mass layoffs in Gaza
stories.summary: UNRWA is laying off staff in Gaza and cutting services, citing a $70 million shortfall. Lead with who loses work and which services stop for Gaza's refugees; then the dispute: laid-off workers, the staff union and a former spokesperson say the cuts aim at the refugee question itself, since UNRWA's existence is what keeps refugee status on record. Name the donors whose withdrawals made the gap.

stories.label: U.S. bombs Iranian island; Israel blocks aid through Rafah; Turkey strikes Al-Shabaab in Somalia
stories.summary: Write only the Rafah item: Israel is blocking aid through the Rafah crossing. Lead with what is held back and how many trucks or people it affects, who decides at the crossing, and what the ceasefire terms say about Rafah. The Qeshm strikes are already covered; leave them and the Somalia item out.

stories.label: Minister accuses politicians of arming thugs to cause violence in 2027
stories.summary: Nigeria's aviation minister Festus Keyamo alleges politicians are arming thugs ahead of the 2027 elections, after parties threatened that anyone who rigs the vote would be killed. Lead with the threat itself and who made it; the mechanism is Nigeria's history of armed political militias in election years. Keep it an allegation: a minister from the ruling party is accusing opponents.

stories.label: Fé VIP e Lagoinha: como plano de Valadão e Vorcaro inflama debate da imunidade de igrejas
stories.summary: Exposed conversations between Lagoinha megachurch leader André Valadão and Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro show a plan that has reopened Brazil's debate on churches' constitutional tax immunity. Lead with what the messages show the two men planned; the mechanism is how religious tax immunity can shelter money with little scrutiny, and a jurist's view on whether the law must change. Accountability story in Latin America.

stories.label: From digital yuan to AI, China signals reach to Oman amid growing strategic ties
stories.summary: During the Sultan of Oman's visit to Beijing, the two agreed to deepen cooperation on BeiDou satellite navigation, AI, the digital economy and the digital yuan. Lead with why Oman matters now: its ports sit outside the Strait of Hormuz while the Iran war closes it, which makes it a hedge for Chinese trade. The mechanism: BeiDou and digital-yuan settlement extend Chinese infrastructure as an alternative to GPS and dollar rails in a Gulf state. Name the yuan.

stories.label: Bitcoin steadies at $76,900 as ETFs lose $399 million and Binance outflows hit $4.7 billion
stories.summary: Net withdrawals from Binance since it reopened have reached $4.7 billion, up from $3.64 billion, while US bitcoin ETFs lost $399 million in a day. Lead with the Binance run and that its promised proof-of-reserves report has still not appeared; the bitcoin price holding near $76,900 is the backdrop, not the story. Name bitcoin.

stories.label: UEFI bootkit infected fully patched Windows machines. Is Microsoft to blame?
stories.summary: A UEFI bootkit, BlackX, infected fully patched Windows machines by bypassing Secure Boot, three years after BlackLotus did the same. Lead with 'fully patched': the fix exists but Microsoft left revoking the vulnerable boot managers optional and unclear, so the chain of trust still accepts them. Explain why malware below the OS survives reinstalls, and who must act: Microsoft, PC makers, admins.

stories.label: Trump wanted to give No Kings no air. Then, Meta suspended its Instagram.
stories.summary: Meta suspended the Instagram account of the No Kings Coalition, one of the largest pro-democracy accounts, around election day, after declining to commit to stopping its automated systems from doing so. Lead with the suspension on voting day; the mechanism is automated moderation that flags surges of activity as abuse, which is exactly when a protest movement's account is busiest. Who holds power: a platform owner courting the White House.

stories.label: Amicro Helped Robot Vacuums Find Their Way. Now It Wants to Go Further.
stories.summary: Zhuhai's Amicro says eight of the world's ten leading cleaning-robot makers, from Xiaomi and Ecovacs to iRobot and Philips, use its navigation chips and software, and it is now seeking a Hong Kong listing. Lead with the hidden dependency: a single Chinese supplier maps the floors of homes worldwide. The mechanism is the component layer of China's robotics industry, and what it plans to move into next.

stories.label: Can China’s clean power stations cope with a changed climate?
stories.summary: China's wind and solar fleet, the world's largest, was sited on past weather, and research now shows wind and sunlight patterns shifting while extreme weather damages equipment. Lead with the measured shift in resource and the failures it has already caused; the mechanism is that climate change erodes the output of the plants built to slow it. Say what experts propose: tougher kit, siting on future rather than past climate, flexible grids.
